title: President
bio: Hon. Roberta Metsola was elected President of the European Parliament in January 2022, becoming the youngest ever person to occupy this role. In July 2024, she was re-elected for another term, as only the second person and first woman to serve as President for two terms. President Metsola has been very vocal and firm in Europe’s support to Ukraine, following Russia’s brutal invasion. On 1st April 2022, she became the first President of an institution of the European Union to visit Ukraine since the start of the war. As President, she has led reforms towards a Parliament that is more modern, efficient and accountable. She was first elected as a Member of the European Parliament in 2013. Prior, President Metsola served within the Permanent Representation of Malta to the European Union and later as the legal advisor to the High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy. In her student years, she campaigned actively for Malta's European Union membership. Professionally she is a lawyer who has specialised in European law and politics. Born in 1979, Roberta Metsola is married to Ukko Metsola and is the mother of four boys.
source_category: sigma.world/summits/world/speakers (Central Europe 2025 + SiGMA World Past speakers)

title: Undersecretary of State
company: Ministry of Economy and Finance of Italy

title: Minister for the Economy, Enterprise and Strategic Projects of Malta
bio: Silvio Schembri, Minister for the Economy, Enterprise and Strategic Projects, is an economist, academic and elected politician. Born in Luqa, he holds a Master’s and Bachelor’s degree in Economics from L-Università ta' Malta. He is experienced in political communication, sustainable development, negotiation and higher education.

title: Leader of the Opposition
bio: "Alex Borg, born on 10 June 1995 in Victoria, Gozo, is a lawyer and politician who currently serves as Leader of the Nationalist Party. He was first elected to the Maltese Parliament in 2022, securing the highest number of votes among Nationalist Party candidates after the party leader at the time. Over the past three years, he has served as Shadow Minister for Gozo and has been a member of both the Parliamentary Committee for Gozo and the Committee for Foreign Affairs. Raised in Nadur, Borg pursued his education at the Bishop's Conservatory, Gozo College, and Sir M. A. Refalo Sixth Form. He graduated with a degree in Law in 2019 and subsequently commenced practice as a lawyer. In 2019, Borg was elected to the Executive of the Nationalist Party Youth Movement, followed shortly thereafter by his election to the Nationalist Party Executive Committee. His commitment to grassroots engagement reflects his conviction that effective politics requires direct and sustained contact between elected representatives and their constituents. Borg's political philosophy centres on fostering a robust and competitive economy while maintaining comprehensive social services. He advocates for a balanced approach that promotes economic growth alongside social equity. Following the resignation of Nationalist Party Leader Dr Bernard Grech in June 2025, Borg announced his candidacy for the leadership position. On 6 September 2025, he was elected Leader of the Nationalist Party, marking a significant milestone in his political trajectory."
source_category: sigma.world/summits/world/speakers (Central Europe 2025 + SiGMA World Past speakers)

title: Member of the Chamber of Deputies
bio: Marcello Coppo is a Member of the Italian Chamber of Deputies with Fratelli d’Italia (Brothers of Italy). A lawyer admitted to the bar in 2009, he advises individuals and businesses on labor, social security, and tax matters. Before his election to Parliament in 2022, he served as Deputy Mayor of Asti (2017–2022) with responsibility for economic development and the promotion of local entrepreneurship, and had previously held various municipal roles in Asti since 2002. In the Chamber of Deputies, he serves on the Public and Private Labour Committee, the Committee on Elections, and the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into workplace conditions and safety. He also serves as Chair of the Inter-Parliamentary Committee on Digital Assets, Blockchain and Bitcoin, engaging with industry and institutions to promote clear, responsible rules for virtual assets that protect consumers while supporting competitiveness and growth.
source_category: sigma.world/summits/world/speakers (Central Europe 2025 + SiGMA World Past speakers)

title: Ambassador of Malta to Italy
bio: Daniel Azzopardi started his career in the Malta Civil Service in 2007 following a Government Scholarship on European Affairs at the University of Sussex, UK. His first post was that of an officer at the Planning and Priorities Coordination Division within the Office of the Prime Minister on the management of EU Funding. In March 2009 he took on his first assignment in Brussels as Technical Attaché in charge of the Energy and Land Transport dossier at the Permanent Representation of Malta to the European Union. He held this position until 2015. At the start of 2016, he returned to Malta as Chief Executive Officer of The Energy and Water Agency, a Government body tasked with developing and implementing Malta’s national policy on energy and water. In 2018 Mr Azzopardi was appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, Permanent Representative of Malta to the European Union. In August 2020 he was then appointed as Malta’s Ambassador to the Kingdom of Spain. Ambassador Azzopardi has been appointed Ambassador to the Italian Republic on 30th August 2024. Ambassador Azzopardi holds a master’s degree in Contemporary European Studies, from the University of Sussex (UK), and a Bachelor of Arts (Hons) in European Studies from the University of Malta. He is married to Dr Roberta Azzopardi and they have 4 children.
source_category: sigma.world/summits/world/speakers (Central Europe 2025 + SiGMA World Past speakers)

Currently serving as Honorary Consul of Brazil in Malta, Founder of Abrama, and Rotarian Board Member, she combines strategic insight with a strong commitment to integrity, stakeholder engagement, and cross-border collaboration.

Now he is Coordinator in the Committee on International Trade for the Socialists and Democrats Group and Chair of the European Parliament's D-US delegation. title: Budget Policy Advisor to the Prime Minister of Italy
bio: Renato Loiero, Parliamentary Advisor to the Senate of the Republic with 23 years of seniority, is currently Budget Policy Advisor to the Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni. He is a member of the technical committee for the implementation of the tax reform. During his service in the Senate, he was initially assigned to the Research Service (economic area), tasked with assisting Committees V (Budget and Economic Planning) and VI (Finance). He was then assigned to the Parliamentary Commissions Service, where he served as a member of the secretariat of Committees V (Budget) and VI (Finance). In the XV legislature, he also served as Head of the Secretariat of the Parliamentary Commission for the Supervision of the Tax Registry. In the XVI legislature, he was also responsible for the Secretariat of the Extraordinary Commission for Price Control. He was president of the Commission for the Quality Assurance of Statistical Information. He is the author of numerous monographs and articles on tax and financial matters. In the past, he also served at the Ministry of Economy and Finance – Lombardy Regional Directorate and as an officer of the Finance Police.

He has conducted research in economic statistics, industrial, international, and regional economics. title: Director General
bio: Since 2011, Antonio Barreca has served as Director General of Federturismo Confindustria, the Italian federation that brings together the entire national tourism industry, representing 23 trade associations. He graduated with honors in Political Science from Luiss Guido Carli, earned a PhD in Comparative Public Law at the University of Perugia (2008), and pursued advanced studies at Harvard’s John F. Kennedy School of Government (2013, 2015). Before his current role, he worked with the Department of Economic Affairs at the Italian Prime Minister’s Office, then spent 10 years in Brussels as Director of Federturismo’s European Affairs Office, engaging with institutions such as the European Economic and Social Committee, the European Commission, and the European Parliament. An academic by vocation, he has taught for more than a decade at Luiss Guido Carli and Luiss Business School—where he also sits on the Scientific Committee of the Master in Tourism Management—as well as other universities. He has held institutional roles as Vice President of the UNI Tourism Commission and special delegate to ISO in Geneva, and served as Special Advisor on Tourism for the Sicilian Region. Currently, he is also Coordinator of the European network of Confindustria tourism federations, Director of AIDIT, and Vice President and co-founder of Turismi.ai. He speaks four languages fluently.

title: Olympic Medalist & Former National Judo Coach of Italy
bio: Felice Mariani is a distinguished Italian sports professional, celebrated both as an elite judoka and as a leader in national and international sporting institutions. A bronze medalist at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, he also earned three World Championship bronzes and three European Championship golds, alongside 11 Italian national titles. Transitioning from athlete to mentor, he has served as Technical Director of the Fiamme Gialle Judo team since 1990 and led the Italian National Judo Team across six Olympic Games, from Seoul to London. Beyond competitive achievements, Mariani served as a Member of the Italian Parliament from March 2018 to October 2022, furthering his commitment to the promotion of sport and social development. Currently collaborating with Sport e Salute, he advances grassroots initiatives nationwide. Recognized as Cavaliere della Repubblica Italiana (1977), inducted into the Judo Hall of Fame (2018), and named Judo Ambassador (2019), he continues to inspire globally.

title: President
bio: Hon. Roberta Metsola was elected President of the European Parliament in January 2022, becoming the youngest ever person to occupy this role. In July 2024, she was re-elected for another term, as only the second person and first woman to serve as President for two terms. President Metsola has been very vocal and firm in Europe’s support to Ukraine, following Russia’s brutal invasion. On 1st April 2022, she became the first President of an institution of the European Union to visit Ukraine since the start of the war. As President, she has led reforms towards a Parliament that is more modern, efficient and accountable. She was first elected as a Member of the European Parliament in 2013. Prior, President Metsola served within the Permanent Representation of Malta to the European Union and later as the legal advisor to the High Representative of the European Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy. In her student years, she campaigned actively for Malta's European Union membership. Professionally she is a lawyer who has specialised in European law and politics. Born in 1979, Roberta Metsola is married to Ukko Metsola and is the mother of four boys.
source_category: sigma.world/summits/world/speakers (Central Europe 2025 + SiGMA World Past speakers)

title: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Italy
bio: Professional journalist since 1980, he has worked as a parliamentary reporter, anchor for GR1 Rai, and head of the Rome newsroom of Il Giornale. Co-founder of Forza Italia, he served as its Vice President from 2018 to 2023 and as National Coordinator from 2021 to 2024. On February 24, 2024, he was unanimously elected National Secretary of Forza Italia. Since 2002, he has been Vice President of the European People’s Party. In 1994, he was elected to the European Parliament for the first time. He was appointed European Commissioner for Transport in 2008, and later Vice President and European Commissioner for Industry and Entrepreneurship in 2010. On January 17, 2017, he was elected President of the European Parliament. From 2019 to 2022, he served as Chair of the Committee on Constitutional Affairs and of the Conference of Committee Chairs of the European Parliament. Since October 22, 2022, he has been Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.

title: Member of the Chamber of Deputies
bio: Marcello Coppo is a Member of the Italian Chamber of Deputies with Fratelli d’Italia (Brothers of Italy). A lawyer admitted to the bar in 2009, he advises individuals and businesses on labor, social security, and tax matters. Before his election to Parliament in 2022, he served as Deputy Mayor of Asti (2017–2022) with responsibility for economic development and the promotion of local entrepreneurship, and had previously held various municipal roles in Asti since 2002. In the Chamber of Deputies, he serves on the Public and Private Labour Committee, the Committee on Elections, and the Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry into workplace conditions and safety. He also serves as Chair of the Inter-Parliamentary Committee on Digital Assets, Blockchain and Bitcoin, engaging with industry and institutions to promote clear, responsible rules for virtual assets that protect consumers while supporting competitiveness and growth.

title: Ambassador of Malta to Italy
bio: Daniel Azzopardi started his career in the Malta Civil Service in 2007 following a Government Scholarship on European Affairs at the University of Sussex, UK. His first post was that of an officer at the Planning and Priorities Coordination Division within the Office of the Prime Minister on the management of EU Funding. In March 2009 he took on his first assignment in Brussels as Technical Attaché in charge of the Energy and Land Transport dossier at the Permanent Representation of Malta to the European Union. He held this position until 2015. At the start of 2016, he returned to Malta as Chief Executive Officer of The Energy and Water Agency, a Government body tasked with developing and implementing Malta’s national policy on energy and water. In 2018 Mr Azzopardi was appointed Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary, Permanent Representative of Malta to the European Union. In August 2020 he was then appointed as Malta’s Ambassador to the Kingdom of Spain. Ambassador Azzopardi has been appointed Ambassador to the Italian Republic on 30th August 2024. Ambassador Azzopardi holds a master’s degree in Contemporary European Studies, from the University of Sussex (UK), and a Bachelor of Arts (Hons) in European Studies from the University of Malta. He is married to Dr Roberta Azzopardi and they have 4 children.
